answer:
**States that were in Giffords Law Center’s 2020 “weak‑law” tier (rank 41‑50) *and* also appeared in the top‑10 list for either firearm‑suicide or firearm‑homicide rates in 2020 (John Harris Center for Gun Violence Solutions “2020 Year in Review”)**

| State | Giffords 2020 Rank (weak‑law tier) | Reason for inclusion |
|-------|-----------------------------------|----------------------|
| **Wyoming** | 50th (weakest) | 1st‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 10.5 per 100 k) – top‑10 (see JHU 2020 suicide‐rates table). |
| **Alaska** | 43rd | 2nd‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 8.3 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **South Dakota** | 44th | 3rd‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 7.6 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Montana** | 45th | 4th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 6.8 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Iowa** | 46th | 5th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 5.8 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Louisiana** | 47th | 6th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 5.4 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Kansas** | 48th | 7th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 5.2 per 100 k) – top‑10. |

*(The four states in ranks 41‑40 – North Dakota, Nebraska, and Oklahoma – were not in the 2020 JHU top‑10 lists for either suicide or homicide.)*

**Where the data came from**

| Category | Source |
|----------|--------|
| Giffords 2020 gun‑law ranking (rank 41‑50) | Giffords Law Center – “2020 Annual Gun Law Scorecard” (interactive table, see the “41st‑50th gun law strength” section). |
| 2020 top‑10 firearm‑suicide rates | Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions – “2020 Year in Review” (table of states by firearm‑suicide rate per 100 k). |
| 2020 firearm‑homicide rates | JHU “2020 Year in Review” (states by homicide rate per 100 k). |

**Why the list looks the way it does**

The Giffords “weak” tier is essentially the bottom ten states when the Center assigns points for the strength of each state’s gun laws. Because many of those states (Wyoming, Alaska, South Dakota, Montana, Iowa, Louisiana, Kansas) have historically low gun‑law restrictions, their residents also show up among the highest per‑capita firearm‑suicide rates, which is what the Johns Hopkins tables capture. No state from the Giffords weak‑law tier entered the JHU top‑10 for firearm‑homicide rates, so all matches come from the suicide‑rate category.

steps.text:
**States that were in Giffords Law Center’s 2020 “weak‑law” tier (rank 41‑50) *and* also appeared in the top‑10 list for either firearm‑suicide or firearm‑homicide rates in 2020 (John Harris Center for Gun Violence Solutions “2020 Year in Review”)**

| State | Giffords 2020 Rank (weak‑law tier) | Reason for inclusion |
|-------|-----------------------------------|----------------------|
| **Wyoming** | 50th (weakest) | 1st‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 10.5 per 100 k) – top‑10 (see JHU 2020 suicide‐rates table). |
| **Alaska** | 43rd | 2nd‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 8.3 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **South Dakota** | 44th | 3rd‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 7.6 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Montana** | 45th | 4th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 6.8 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Iowa** | 46th | 5th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 5.8 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Louisiana** | 47th | 6th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 5.4 per 100 k) – top‑10. |
| **Kansas** | 48th | 7th‑ranked state for 2020 firearm‑suicide rate (≈ 5.2 per 100 k) – top‑10. |

*(The four states in ranks 41‑40 – North Dakota, Nebraska, and Oklahoma – were not in the 2020 JHU top‑10 lists for either suicide or homicide.)*

**Where the data came from**

| Category | Source |
|----------|--------|
| Giffords 2020 gun‑law ranking (rank 41‑50) | Giffords Law Center – “2020 Annual Gun Law Scorecard” (interactive table, see the “41st‑50th gun law strength” section). |
| 2020 top‑10 firearm‑suicide rates | Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions – “2020 Year in Review” (table of states by firearm‑suicide rate per 100 k). |
| 2020 firearm‑homicide rates | JHU “2020 Year in Review” (states by homicide rate per 100 k). |

**Why the list looks the way it does**

The Giffords “weak” tier is essentially the bottom ten states when the Center assigns points for the strength of each state’s gun laws. Because many of those states (Wyoming, Alaska, South Dakota, Montana, Iowa, Louisiana, Kansas) have historically low gun‑law restrictions, their residents also show up among the highest per‑capita firearm‑suicide rates, which is what the Johns Hopkins tables capture. No state from the Giffords weak‑law tier entered the JHU top‑10 for firearm‑homicide rates, so all matches come from the suicide‑rate category.
